title: Internal and External Advertisement for the Positions of Registrar and Bursar
excerpt: 1.0 PREAMBLE The Governing Council of Lagos State University hereby announces that the positions of Registrar and Bursar will be vacant in July 2026.
content:
1.0 PREAMBLE

The Governing Council of Lagos State University hereby announces that the positions of Registrar and Bursar will be vacant in July 2026.

In consonance with the Lagos State University Law 2004 (As amended), and in exercise of the powers contained therein, the Governing Council has decided to begin the process of appointing new Registrar and Bursar.

Consequently, applications are hereby invited from suitably

qualified applicants for the positions of Registrar and Bursar.

2.0 THE INSTITUTION

Lagos State University (LASU) was established in 1983 by the Enabling Law of Lagos State of Nigeria, for the advancement of learning, establishment of academic excellence AND to meet the specific manpower needs of Lagos State, as well as undertake any other activities appropriate for a university of the highest standard.

Lagos State University is reputed for high standards, which it

has maintained over the years and is currently ranked amongst the foremost universities in the country.

The University currently has sixteen (16) Faculties, six (6) Schools, Nine (9) Centres, and three (3) Institutes, spread across the four (4) campuses of the University.

1. THE UNIVERSITY REGISTRAR

In accordance with the Lagos State University Law 2004 (As

amended), the Registrar is a Principal Officer and is responsible to the Vice-Chancellor for the day-to-day administration of the affairs of the University, except financial matters which fall within the jurisdiction of the Bursar. The Registrar is the Head of the University Registry.

Eligibility Criteria and Experience

Candidates must possess the following:

▪A good honours degree from a recognised institution;

▪Fifteen (15) years relevant administrative experience in University administration;

▪A relevant higher degree;

▪A minimum of five (5) years as a Deputy Registrar in a recognised tertiary institution;

▪Proficiency in the use of ICT for management services; and

▪Membership of Association of Nigerian University Professional Administrators (ANUPA) and relevant professional associations.

Key Responsibilities

▪Serve as Secretary to Council, Senate,

Congregation and Convocation;

▪Interpret, guide and advise appropriate bodies on the regulations of the University as contained in the Conditions of Service;

▪Manage the human and material resources to ensure good administration;

▪Oversee institutional records, official correspondence and regulatory documentation;

▪Ensure compliance with University policies,

government regulations and accreditation standards;

▪Promote effective communication between Faculties, University Management and internal/external stakeholders; and

▪Any other responsibilities as may be assigned by

the Vice-Chancellor.

2. THE UNIVERSITY BURSAR

In accordance with the Lagos State University Law 2004 (As amended), the Bursar is a Principal Officer and is responsible to the Vice-Chancellor for the day-to-day administration and control of financial affairs of the

University, across its campuses. The Bursar is the Head of

the University Bursary.

Eligibility Criteria and Experience

Candidates must possess the following:

▪A good honours degree/Higher National

Diploma (HND) in Accounting from a

recognised institution;

▪Fifteen (15) years relevant post-qualification

experience plus professional qualification of

ICAN/ACA/ACMA/ANAN with twelve

(12) years relevant post-qualification experience;

▪A relevant higher degree;

▪Proficiency in the use of relevant accounting software;

▪Proficiency in the use of AI tools; and

▪A minimum of five (5) years as a Deputy Bursar in a

recognised tertiary institution.

Key Responsibilities

▪Develop and manage the University's annual

budget and ensure financial discipline;

▪Supervise financial reporting, treasury

operations, and internal control systems;

▪Oversee the Bursary Department and all financial

transactions;

▪Implement cost-efficiency strategies and

optimise resource utilisation;

▪Advise the Vice-Chancellor and Governing Council

on financial matters, including risk management; and

▪Any other responsibilities that may be assigned by the Vice-Chancellor.

3.0 TENURE

In consonance with the Lagos State University Law 2004 (As amended), the appointment of Registrar or Bursar is for a TERM of four (4) years, respectively, with eligibility for reappointment for a second term of four

(4) years ONLY.

4.0 AGE REQUIREMENT

Candidates for the position of Registrar or Bursar must not

be above the age of sixty (60) years by July, 2026.

5.0 REMUNERATION

Remuneration of the Registrar or Bursar at Lagos State University includes Basic Salary of CONUNASS 15 AND other benefits AND allowances that apply to the Registrar and Bursar in Nigerian public universities, as may be approved by the Governing Council, Lagos State University.

6.0 METHOD OF APPLICATION

Candidates should submit formal Application for the posts of:

1. Registrar

2. Bursar

Candidates should apply with Fifteen (15) copies of their detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV), providing information on the following:

• Full Name

• Place AND Date of Birth

• Nationality (If Nigerian, indicate State of Origin)

• Marital Status: Number AND Ages of Children

• Academic Qualifications (including Class of Degree;

copies of certificates to be enclosed)

• Professional Qualifications (copies of certificates to be

enclosed)

• Statement of Experience including details of former and

present positions

• Names AND Addresses of Three (3) Referees, who should be able to attest to the candidate’s character, professional and managerial skills

• Contact Address (including telephone number(s) AND

e-mail address)

7.0 SUBMISSION OF APPLICATION

All applications are to be submitted under CONFIDENTIAL

COVER, with the envelope marked “POST OF

REGISTRAR or POST OF BURSAR” (whichever is

applicable), sealed, addressed AND submitted to:

The Vice-Chancellor,

Vice-Chancellor’s Office,

Babatunde Raji Fashola Senate Building, Lagos State University,

Badagry Expressway,

Ojo, Lagos, Nigeria.

Kindly NOTE that the application should reach the Vice-Chancellor NOT later than six (6) weeks from the date

of this publication.

8.0 SHORTLISTED CANDIDATES

Shortlisted candidates will be required to make

themselves available for interview with the Selection Board at a DATE that will be formally conveyed to such candidates in writing.

title: Advertisement for Part-Time and Full-Time Admission into Postgraduate Programmes for the 2025/2026 Academic Session
excerpt: The Postgraduate School invites applications from suitably qualified applicants for admission into the underlisted postgraduate programmes at the Lagos State University (LASU), Ojo, for the 2025/2026 academic session.
content:
The Postgraduate School invites applications from suitably qualified applicants for admission into the underlisted postgraduate programmes at the Lagos State University (LASU), Ojo, for the 2025/2026 academic session.

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

The University requires Five (5) CREDITS including English Language at Ordinary Level (GCE, WASC, SSCE, GRADE II CERT., NECO and NABTEB) for ALL courses and credit in MATHEMATICS at Ordinary Level for SCIENCE, SOCIAL SCIENCES, MANAGEMENT SCIENCES and EDUCATIONAL MANAGEMENT courses.

METHOD OF APPLICATION

Applicants are required to pay the sum of Thirty Thousand, Three Hundred Naira (N30,300.00) non-refundable application fee into LASU Account online.

All applicants shall be required to sit for qualifying Entrance Examination at the Lagos State University Main Campus, Ojo, Lagos.

NOTE: Visit the university website

www.lasu.edu.ng for information on admission requirements.

CLOSING DATE

Sale of application forms will be closed four [4] weeks from the date of this publication.

Application forms for all programmes should be submitted online and a copy of the e-Registration slip should be printed out by the applicant.

NOTE:

1. Applicants who have not completed the National Youth Service Corps assignment or their current Postgraduate Programmes need not apply;

2. All academic transcripts must be received latest two (2) weeks after the close of sale of forms;

3. Request for transfer of processed application forms from one Department to another will not be entertained;

4. Applicants must personally attend the selection and written examinations as make-up test will not be conducted; and

5. Applicants are to include their e-mail addresses/phone numbers on the application form.

STEPS FOR POSTGRADUATE APPLICATION

1. Visit https://studentservices.lasu.edu.ng/pg_application/newstudents/

2. Click on “Step 1” to generate an Application Number;

3. Supply basic bio-data details and select Postgraduate Programme Dropdown;

4. Click Continue;

5. An Application Number will be generated. Copy the Application Number generated;

6. Proceed to “Step 2” make the required payment for the Postgraduate Application Fee;

7. After successful payment, return to the application page on “Step 3” to continue the Application;

8. Supply Application Number and Surname;

9. Complete all required information; and

10. Print out your application form.

For further information, please contact:

The Senior Deputy Registrar/Secretary,

Postgraduate School,

Lagos State University, Ojo, Lagos.

Secretary-pgs@lasu.edu.ng

title: Alumni Spotlight: Mr Hakeem Muri-Okunola — Principal Secretary to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
excerpt: Mr Hakeem Muri-Okunola is a seasoned public administrator and legal practitioner who currently serves as Principal Secretary to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.
content:
Mr Hakeem Muri-Okunola is a seasoned public administrator and legal practitioner who currently serves as Principal Secretary to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

He is a graduate of Lagos State University (LASU), where he obtained a Bachelor of Law (LL.B) degree in 1995, and was subsequently called to the Nigerian Bar. He further earned a Master of Laws (LL.M) in International Business Law from Queen Mary and Westfield College, University of London, England.

His grounding in Law and Public Administration laid the foundation for a career defined by diligence, institutional depth and steady progression within government service.

Mr Muri-Okunola, also known as “HMO”, served as Personal Assistant to then - Governor Bola Tinubu between 2003 and 2005. He was subsequently appointed Executive Secretary of the Land Use and Allocation Committee.

Afterwards he became a Permanent Secretary in the Lagos State Public Service in 2011 and was posted to the Lands Bureau in the Governor’s Office where he supervised the State’s Lands Administration machinery. In 2015, he was named Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Youth and Social Development.

Three years down the line, precisely December 30, 2018, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu appointed him as the 21st Head of Service of Lagos State - becoming the youngest person to hold the office at 46. In that role, he oversaw the state’s Civil Service architecture and institutional reforms.

In September 2023, he transitioned to the national stage, accepting the role of Principal Secretary to President Bola Tinubu at the Federal Government of Nigeria.

Over the course of his career, Chief Muri-Okunola has been recognised for his administrative discipline, meticulousness, organisational oversight and commitment to strengthening governance structures.

title: LASU Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor Congratulate Alumnus, Mr Tunji Disu, on his Appointment as Acting Inspector General of Police
excerpt: The Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council of Lagos State University (LASU), Mr Babatunde OGALA, SAN, OFR, together with the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM, on behalf of the Governing...
content:
The Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council of Lagos State University (LASU), Mr Babatunde OGALA, SAN, OFR, together with the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM, on behalf of the Governing Council, Management, staff, students, and alumni of the University, warmly congratulate a distinguished alumnus, Mr Tunji DISU, on his appointment as the Acting Inspector General of Police of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

Mr DISU, whose appointment was announced by the Presidency on Tuesday, 24th February 2026, holds a Bachelor’s Degree (B.A.) in English Education, as well as Master’s degrees in Public Administration and in Criminology, Security, and Legal Psychology from Lagos State University.

The appointment, which is well deserved and meritorious, is a powerful testament to Mr DISU’s integrity, professional competence, and decades of disciplined and patriotic service to our nation.

The Pro-Chancellor and the Vice-Chancellor affirmed that Mr DISU represents the very best of LASU – resilient, intellectually grounded, and committed to transformational leadership. His elevation to the highest office in the Nigeria Police Force reinforces the University’s standing as a breeding ground for leaders who shape institutions and drive national progress.

They expressed confidence that the Acting Inspector General would deploy his intellectual depth, vast operational experience, and strategic insight to strengthen reforms, deepen public trust, and enhance service delivery within the Nigeria Police Force.

As he assumes leadership at a pivotal moment for national security, the University community celebrates this milestone achievement and wishes him great wisdom, courage, and success in office.

title: LASU Pledges Stronger Support for Student-Led Initiatives as Hult Prize, JCI Team Visit Vice-Chancellor
excerpt: ‎Lagos State University (LASU) has pledged stronger support for student-led initiatives following separate courtesy visits by the Hult Prize and Junior Chamber International (JCI) LASU Chapter to the Vice-Chancellor, Professor...
content:
‎Lagos State University (LASU) has pledged stronger support for student-led initiatives following separate courtesy visits by the Hult Prize and Junior Chamber International (JCI) LASU Chapter to the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, mni, NPOM, on Wednesday, 25th February 2026 at the Vice-Chancellor’s Conference Room, 6th Floor, Babatunde Raji Fashola Senate Building, Main Campus, Ojo.

‎The student delegations visited the Vice-Chancellor to present their initiatives and explore avenues for deeper institutional collaboration aimed at expanding student development opportunities.

‎The Hult Prize delegation, led by Campus Director Sheriffdeen Ashiru, a 300-level Computer Science student, commended the Vice-Chancellor’s administration for what he described as significant milestones achieved since she assumed office. He noted that the progress recorded under her leadership has fostered a conducive academic environment that supports innovation, enterprise, and student-led initiatives.

‎He described the Hult Prize as an annual global competition that challenges young people to develop scalable and sustainable social enterprises capable of addressing some of the world’s most pressing challenges. He highlighted the team’s activities on campus, outlined operational challenges, and formally sought enhanced collaboration with the University, to enable more LASU students to benefit from the global opportunities offered by the initiative.

‎Responding on behalf of the Vice-Chancellor, the Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Academics, Professor Oseni Taiwo Afisi, FSPSP, applauded the team’s vision and commitment. He observed that their drive reflects the leadership potential inherent in LASU students and aligns with the University’s aspiration to produce globally competitive graduates. ‎He encouraged the team to remain focused and ambitious, noting that they are already demonstrating the traits of world-class students. Professor Afisi assured them of the University’s readiness to provide the necessary support to strengthen their activities and broaden their impact.

‎Shortly after, the Junior Chamber International (JCI) LASU Chapter also paid a courtesy visit to the Vice-Chancellor. The delegation was led by the current Chapter President, Miss Suliat Mogaji, a 300-level Philosophy student.

‎In her address, Miss Mogaji expressed appreciation to the University leadership for creating an enabling environment that allows student organisations to thrive. She thanked the Vice-Chancellor for her consistent support and requested further institutional backing to enable JCI to reach more students, scale up its programmes, and deepen its positive impact within and beyond the campus community.

‎In his response, Professor Afisi commended the team and their contributions to leadership development and community engagement within the University. He urged them to intensify awareness campaigns to ensure broader student participation in JCI activities and reaffirmed the University’s commitment to providing the access and support required for the organisation to achieve its objectives.

‎At the end of the visits, both teams made gift presentations to the Vice-Chancellor.

‎In attendance was the Chief Public Relations Officer/Head, Media Relations Unit, Centre for Information and Public Relations, Mr Olaniyi Jeariogbe who serves as staff adviser for both organisations.

‎The visits concluded with a vote of thanks delivered on behalf of the Registrar, Mr Emmanuel A. Fanu, by the Deputy Registrar/Special Assistant to the Vice-Chancellor, Dr Lateef Salami.

title: LASU Management Pays Familiarisation Visit to New Chancellor, HRM Oba Olufolarin Ogunsanwo, as Monarch Pledges to be a Father Figure to University
excerpt: The Vice-Chancellor of Lagos State University, Prof. Ibiyemi Ibilola Olatunji-Bello, mni, NPOM, on Thursday, 19th February 2026, led members of the University Management team on a familiarisation visit to the institution’s newly...
content:
The Vice-Chancellor of Lagos State University, Prof. Ibiyemi Ibilola Olatunji-Bello, mni, NPOM, on Thursday, 19th February 2026, led members of the University Management team on a familiarisation visit to the institution’s newly appointed Chancellor, HRM Oba Dr Olufolarin Olukayode Ogunsanwo, at his palace in Epe Kingdom.

Oba Ogunsanwo, the Alara of Ilara Epe, was recently appointed as the 6th Chancellor of LASU by the Governor of Lagos State, Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu, following the expiration of the tenure of the immediate past Chancellor, Prof. Gbolahan Elias, SAN.

Addressing the paramount ruler, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Olatunji-Bello said the delegation was at the palace to formally pay homage and congratulate the new Chancellor on his appointment.

The professor of Physiology noted that the monarch’s ascension to the noble office reflected not only his distinguished royal heritage but also his unwavering commitment to scholarship, leadership and service to humanity.

“Your ascension to this noble office reflects not only your distinguished royal heritage but also your commitment to scholarship, leadership and service to humanity,” she stated. “As the Alara of Ilara Epe, you have demonstrated leadership rooted in tradition and community development. We are confident that these same virtues will enrich and elevate Lagos State University.”

Describing the new Chancellor as a bridge between heritage and innovation, Prof. Olatunji-Bello added, “With you, we see a custodian of values and a father figure whose guidance will continue to strengthen the moral fabric of LASU. Your depth of experience and exposure will undoubtedly inspire our students to pursue excellence not only in academia but also in character and lifelong learning.”

In his response, Oba Ogunsanwo expressed gratitude to God for the appointment and thanked Governor Sanwo-Olu for finding him worthy of the responsibility, which he said he accepted with humility, honour and respect.

He noted that he was not a stranger to LASU, having obtained a Master’s degree from the University in 1995 and being currently enrolled in a PhD in Business Administration. “My joy is that your products are now being sent back to you to be of value,” he said.

The monarch paid tribute to his predecessors, particularly Prof. Gbolahan Elias, SAN, commending their contributions to the growth of the University in collaboration with past and present Vice-Chancellors.

“I will give my all, my knowledge, goodwill and experience, to ensure that we take LASU to a position of reckoning in the world,” he pledged. “I will be a father figure and a face for LASU, so that when we look back, we will thank God.”

He further assured the Management of his commitment to exploring broader opportunities for collaboration, including in artificial intelligence, and attracting well-meaning Nigerians to support the continued development of the University.

Oba Ogunsanwo was in the company of his wife, Olori Bolanle Ogunsanwo, other traditional rulers of surrounding kingdoms- HRM Oba Ayodele Aliru, the Alade of Uraka Poka Land and HRM Oba Adelani Adeniyi Oke, the Adegbajo of Odo-Gbawojo Kingdom as well as the Alara-in-Council of Ilara, the Baale-in-Council of Ilara and other well-wishers.

Members of the LASU Management team on the visit included the Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Academics, Prof. Oseni Afisi; Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Administration, Prof. Oluwatoyin Enikuomehin; the Registrar, Mr Emmanuel Fanu; the Bursar, Mr Said Babatunde Olayinka; and the University Librarian, Dr Olawunmi Makinde.

Also present were the Deputy Registrar, Vice-Chancellor’s Office, Dr Lateef Shekoni; Deputy Registrar/Special Assistant to the Vice-Chancellor, Dr Lateef Salami; Deputy Registrar/Head, Council Affairs Division, Mr Oladele Olorunfunmi; Deputy Registrar/ Coordinator, Centre for Information and Public Relations, Mrs Oluwayemisi Thomas-Onashile; Admissions Officer, Mr Agboola Bamgboye; Media Aide to the Vice-Chancellor, Mr Oluwaseun Gbanja; Personal Assistant to the Vice-Chancellor, Mrs Fatima Ogunniyi; Administrative Officer I, Mr Bisiriyu Obasa; Administrative Officer II, Mr Tunji Salami; and Mrs Grace Ologeh.

The official investiture of the Chancellor will take place at a yet-to-be-announced date.

title: Appointment of the 6th Chancellor of Lagos State University
excerpt: The Governor of Lagos State and Visitor to Lagos State University, Mr Babajide Olusola SANWO-OLU, has appointed His Royal Majesty, Oba (Dr) Olufolarin Olukayode OGUNSANWO, the Alara of Ilara, as the 6th Chancellor of Lagos State...
content:
The Governor of Lagos State and Visitor to Lagos State University, Mr Babajide Olusola SANWO-OLU, has appointed His Royal Majesty, Oba (Dr) Olufolarin Olukayode OGUNSANWO, the Alara of Ilara, as the 6th Chancellor of Lagos State University (LASU).

This appointment follows the completion of the tenure of Professor Gbolahan ELIAS, SAN, who served meritoriously as the 5th Chancellor of the University. The Lagos State Government and the entire University community appreciate his contributions to the University and the dignity with which he represented the University throughout his tenure.

The appointment is made pursuant to the provisions of the Lagos State University Law 2004 (As amended), Chapter L69, Volume 7, Schedule 1, which empowers the Visitor to appoint the Chancellor of the University.

His Majesty’s appointment is for a single term of Five (5) years, effective from Friday, 13th February 2026, and is renewable once.

The Pro-Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor warmly congratulate HRM Oba (Dr) Olufolarin Olukayode OGUNSANWO on this distinguished appointment and look forward to his impactful leadership in advancing the vision and mission of Lagos State University.

title: NUC Teams Impressed with LASU after Resource Assessment and Accreditation Exercise
excerpt: The National Universities Commission (NUC) teams have expressed satisfaction and commendation for Lagos State University (LASU) following the successful conduct of a resource assessment and accreditation exercise at the institution.
content:
The National Universities Commission (NUC) teams have expressed satisfaction and commendation for Lagos State University (LASU) following the successful conduct of a resource assessment and accreditation exercise at the institution.

This was contained in the teams’ reports presented during an exit meeting with the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM, and other Principal Officers. The meeting was held at the Conference Room of the Vice-Chancellor’s Office, Sixth Floor, Babatunde Raji Fashola Senate Building, Main Campus, Ojo, Lagos, on Monday, 9th February 2026.

In their separate reports, members of the NUC teams applauded the University for its remarkable development and growth, based on the facilities and resources inspected. They, however, highlighted certain areas where further improvements were required.

Responding, the Vice-Chancellor expressed appreciation to the teams for what she described as a painstaking peer review exercise. She assured them that Management had carefully noted their observations and would take the necessary steps to address them.

Earlier in the day, while formally receiving the NUC Resource Assessment and Accreditation teams at the Senate Chamber, Professor OLATUNJI-BELLO informed the visitors that the University Management was fully prepared for the dual exercise involving resource assessment and accreditation of selected academic programmes.

She described the exercise as a critical component of quality assurance and reiterated Management’s commitment to academic excellence and the holistic development of students. According to her, LASU produces highly intelligent and resourceful graduates.

“LASU combines both physical and virtual learning in teaching students. We equally deploy e-resources to support learning. LASU remains the most advanced digital state university in Nigeria. We recognise that this exercise is a peer review, and we are fully prepared and hopeful of success. You will receive full support from the Faculties and maximum cooperation,” she stated.

The Vice-Chancellor concluded her remarks by encouraging members of the teams to take time to experience the attractions of Lagos, including its beaches, lagoon, and the Blue Rail Line.

Speaking on behalf of the NUC teams, the Team Lead for Special Education, Professor Ajibade OYELOYE, described LASU and the Commission as partners in progress. He emphasised that the exercise was a peer review and not a witch-hunt, and assured that the teams would carry out their duties diligently and make recommendations where necessary.

Similarly, the Representative of the Executive Secretary, NUC, Mrs Roseline ODUEKA, affirmed that the teams would discharge their responsibilities objectively, adding that their ultimate goal was to contribute towards making LASU a better institution. She also commended the University Management for the warm hospitality extended to the teams.

In his remarks, Professor Bassey ESU noted that the exercise was designed to validate available resources, expressing confidence that LASU had exceeded the Commission’s expectations.

Following the opening session, the Vice-Chancellor formally handed over the teams to the Deans of the concerned Faculties.

Principal Officers present at the event included the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academics), Professor Oseni AFISI; Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Administration), Professor Toyin ENUKUOMEHIN; University Registrar, Mr Emmanuel A. FANU; University Bursar, Mr Said Babatunde OLAYINKA; and the University Librarian, Dr Omawumi MAKINDE.

Deans in attendance were Professor Jide JIMOH (Faculty of Communication and Media Studies), Professor Gbenga AKINDOJU (Faculty of Education), Professor Tunji AZEEZ (Faculty of Creativity, Culture and Tourism), Dr Abayomi ADELEKE (Faculty of Library, Archival and Information Science), Professor Isaiah AKOTEYON (Faculty of Environmental Sciences), and Professor Akanji BANKOLE (Faculty of Management Sciences). The Director of Academic Planning, Dr Morenikeji OLANREWAJU-JOHN, moderated the session.

Programmes presented for accreditation included Special Education, Architecture, and Library and Information Science, while the following programmes were presented for resource verification: Broadcasting, Information and Media, Tourism and Hospitality Management, Public Relations and Strategic Communication, Advertising and Development Communication, Entrepreneurship, Film Production, and Journalism/Multimedia.

title: Alumni Spotlight: HRM Oba Saheed Ademola Elegushi, Kusenla III, the 21st Elegushi of Ikate‑Elegushi Kingdom
excerpt: HRM Oba Saheed Ademola Elegushi’s journey from a dedicated student at Lagos State University (LASU) to one of Lagos State’s most influential traditional rulers is a story of leadership, service, and lifelong learning. His formal...
content:
HRM Oba Saheed Ademola Elegushi’s journey from a dedicated student at Lagos State University (LASU) to one of Lagos State’s most influential traditional rulers is a story of leadership, service, and lifelong learning. His formal education at St. Mathias Primary School in Lagos and Methodist Boys’ High School, laid a strong foundation for his academic and professional pursuits.

At LASU, he studied Economics from 1995 to 2000, graduating with a second class honours B.Sc. He remained at LASU to complete a Master’s degree in Economics (2002–2003) before broadening his global perspective at the University of Manchester (Manchester Business School) in the United Kingdom, where he earned a Master’s in Public Administration.

Before ascending the throne as the 21st Elegushi of Ikate‑Elegushi Kingdom in 2010, Oba Elegushi built a notable career in public service and strategy. He gained experience as an administrator in business development and then served as Personal Assistant to former Lagos State Governor Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu and later Senior Special Assistant on Special Duties to then Governor Babatunde Raji Fashola, SAN.

In 2023, LASU honoured him with an Honorary Doctor of Arts in Broadcasting, Community Integration and Human Rights Advocacy, acknowledging his broad impact on society and reaffirming his deep ties to his alma mater.

Prior to that, he’d been awarded an honorary doctorate in Public Administration by Igbinedion University, Okada, Edo State and European-American University in Public Leadership, Peace, and Community Development.

Elegushi’s reign is marked by transformative community initiatives: from health outreach and infrastructure improvements in Ikateland to educational support for indigent students and the establishment of historical research centres that spotlight the evolution of Lagos society.

title: LASU’S Best Graduating Law Student, Toheeb Omotayo Alimi, Wins Prestigious Bosan 2025 Scholarship
excerpt: The Lagos State University’s Best Graduating Student in the Faculty of Law for the 2024/2025 Academic Session, Toheeb Omotayo Alimi, has emerged as a recipient of the 2025 Body of Senior Advocates of Nigeria (BOSAN) Scholarship...
content:
The Lagos State University’s Best Graduating Student in the Faculty of Law for the 2024/2025 Academic Session, Toheeb Omotayo Alimi, has emerged as a recipient of the 2025 Body of Senior Advocates of Nigeria (BOSAN) Scholarship Award, valued at one million naira (₦1,000,000).

The prestigious scholarship, instituted by the Body of Senior Advocates of Nigeria (BOSAN), forms part of a strategic national initiative aimed at reversing the declining standards in legal education and professional practice in Nigeria. The scheme targets exceptional law students at both university and Nigerian Law School levels, setting measurable standards that promote academic excellence, character, discipline, and professional integrity.

Following a rigorous national selection process, Alimi was named one of the successful awardees for 2025, a distinction that places him among Nigeria’s most promising emerging legal minds.

According to the official award notification, the scholarship will be disbursed in two phases:

₦500,000 during his final year at the university

₦500,000 during his attendance at the Nigerian Law School

Beyond the financial support, the BOSAN Scholarship carries significant professional prestige. Beneficiaries are formally recognised as BOSAN Scholars, a distinction that confers honour not only within their universities and the Nigerian Law School, but throughout their future legal careers.

The formal award ceremony is scheduled to take place at the 50th Anniversary Dinner of the Conferment of the Rank of Senior Advocates of Nigeria, on Saturday, 7th February 2026, at Harbour Point, 4 Wilmot Point Road, off Ahmadu Bello Road, Victoria Island, Lagos State.

The scholarship scheme also maintains strict standards of accountability, with BOSAN emphasising that any beneficiary who falls below the required academic, conduct, or character standards risks the immediate withdrawal of the award.

For LASU, the recognition of Alimi represents a powerful affirmation of its commitment to producing legal professionals of exceptional quality and integrity. For the Nigerian legal profession, it signals a renewed investment in building a new generation of lawyers grounded in excellence, ethics, and service.

title: LASU to host Landmark Global Psychology Conference, a First for Nigeria
excerpt: Lagos State University has been confirmed as the host of the 11th International Conference of Community Psychology (ICCP 2026), scheduled to take place from 28th August to 7th September 2026, marking a historic milestone as the...
content:
Lagos State University has been confirmed as the host of the 11th International Conference of Community Psychology (ICCP 2026), scheduled to take place from 28th August to 7th September 2026, marking a historic milestone as the first time the conference will be hosted in Nigeria, with Lagos State University taking the lead role.

The announcement was made on Monday, 12th January 2026, during a press conference addressed by the Vice-Chancellor of Lagos State University, Professor Ibiyemi Ibilola OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM.

Professor Olatunji-Bello, in in her address, averred: “This conference provides a historic opportunity for Africa to reconnect global psychological practice to indigenous wisdom, collective resilience, and community-centred solutions,” she declared.

She described the hosting of ICCP 2026 as a major academic and national achievement that places Nigeria more firmly within global conversations on community-centred psychological science.

The theme of the international conference, “Gathering in the Motherland: Celebrating Ways of the Waters and Reconnecting to the Source", which has been structured into three phases:

a. Pre-conference activities from 28th to 30th August 2026;

b. Main conference from 1st to 4th September 2026; and

c. Post-conference engagements from 5th to 7th September 2026.

Professor Olatunji-Bello emphasised that the discipline of Community Psychology goes beyond individual-level interventions to address systemic issues like such as inequality and mental health through collaborative, community-driven approaches.

She highlighted Lagos State's readiness as Nigeria’s safest commercial hub, a centre of excellence known for innovation and diversity, and affirmed that LASU’s strong tradition of scholarship makes it an ideal host.

The Vice-Chancellor assured that delegates from all over the world would experience both high-level academic discourse and the cultural richness of Lagos. The event is organised in partnership with the Nigerian Psychological Association and the Pan-African Psychology Union and has gained endorsements from bodies worldwide, including the American Psychological Association.

Addressing safety and inclusivity, the Vice-Chancellor stated that comprehensive arrangements with the State and security agencies are in place to ensure a secure and accessible environment for all participants, including those with disabilities and diverse identities.

The press conference featured a unified front of university and community leadership, where other key speakers reinforced the importance of the event.

A Member of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Honourable Solomon BONU; the Chairman of the Nigeria Labour Congress, Comrade (Chief) Funmi Agnes SESSI; and the President of the Pan-African Psychology Union (PAPU), Professor Andrew ZAMANI, were joined by some members of the conference's Local Organising Committee (LOC), including the Alternate Chairperson, Professor Temitayo D. ADEWUYI, as well as the Convener of ICCP, from the United States of America, Dr Moshood OLANREWAJU. Together, they underscored the conference's broad significance, stating that hosting ICCP 2026 would strengthen LASU’s global profile, promote Africa’s intellectual contributions, stimulate local economic activity and tourism, and help reshape dominant narratives in psychological knowledge.

Professor Olatunji-Bello concluded by calling on the media, corporate organisations, and development partners to support the conference through sponsorships, framing it as a platform for global collaboration and national opportunity. She offered a firm reassurance: “Lagos State is safe, welcoming, and ready to receive the world.” With this historic event, LASU proudly affirms its place on the global stage.

Members of Lagos State University Management were all in attendance.

title: Abolition of Paper‑Based Memoranda and Mandatory Adoption of the LASU Electronic Memo system (LASU-eMS)
excerpt: The Management of Lagos State University, acting on the directive of the Vice‑Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi Ibilola Olatunji‑Bello, hereby announces the mandatory abolition of paper‑based memoranda across all spheres of University...
content:
The Management of Lagos State University, acting on the directive of the Vice‑Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi Ibilola Olatunji‑Bello, hereby announces the mandatory abolition of paper‑based memoranda across all spheres of University operations, including academic, administrative, and support units.

This directive takes effect from 1st February 2026. From this date, all new official internal memoranda shall be initiated, processed, and concluded exclusively through the Lagos State University Electronic Memorandum System (LASU‑eMS). A two‑week transition period, from 1st February to 14th February 2026, has been approved solely for clearing existing paper‑based memoranda already in circulation. Beginning 15th February 2026, paper‑based memoranda shall no longer be accepted or processed.

In preparation for full implementation, training for all stakeholders and users has been scheduled to take place throughout January 2026, to ensure that staff across all units are adequately equipped to use the system effectively ahead of the commencement date.

The Vice‑Chancellor has formally directed the adoption of LASU-eMS as the sole official memorandum‑processing platform of the University and has commended the Directorate of Information and Communication Technology for this major institutional achievement. LASU-eMS is a fully home‑grown application, conceptualised, developed, and deployed internally by the University, reflecting LASU’s administrative structure, approval hierarchy, and operational realities.

Why Paper‑Based Memoranda Are Being Abolished

The use of paper‑based memoranda has over time presented significant administrative challenges, including delays in memo movement, difficulty in tracking documents, misplaced or unattended files, lack of audit trails, duplication of effort, and inflexible processes. These limitations have adversely affected efficiency, transparency, and timely decision‑making.

With the deployment of LASU-eMS, these challenges will now become a thing of the past. Memo tracking is seamless and transparent, the treatment of memos is faster and more flexible, and officers are able to act promptly without the constraints of physical document movement.

Key Advantages of LASU-eMS

The adoption of LASU-eMS delivers clear institutional benefits, including:

- Faster and more transparent processing of memos

- Easy and real‑time tracking of all memoranda

- Improved flexibility in memo treatment and approvals

- Clear accountability through comprehensive audit trails

- Elimination of lost, delayed, or forgotten memos

- Secure handling of confidential communications

- Reduced paper usage, storage challenges, and operational costs

- Improved institutional record management and compliance

Compliance and Support

All staff are required to comply fully with this directive. Any deviation will be regarded as non‑compliance with approved administrative procedures.

The Directorate of Information and Communication Technology will provide continuous support, user guides, and hands‑on training throughout the scheduled training period to ensure smooth and effective adoption.

Conclusion

The mandatory adoption of LASU-eMS represents a major leap in administrative efficiency, accountability, and digital governance at Lagos State University. It further reinforces the University’s standing as a national leader in technology‑driven administration and institutional innovation.

All members of the University community are enjoined to cooperate fully to ensure the success of this initiative.

The Lagos State University Disability Support Office on Wednesday, 3rd December 2025, celebrated the 2025 United Nations International Day of Persons with Disabilities with the theme: *“Fostering Disability Inclusive Societies for Advancing Social Progress.”

The Disability Support Office organised a rally to create awareness among members of the university community and students with special needs on campus. The rally commenced and concluded at the frontage of the Babatunde Raji Fashola Senate Building, Main Campus, Ojo, Lagos.

Before the rally, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, mni, NPOM, represented by the Registrar, Mr Emmanuel FANU, addressed the students at the Senate Chamber, Babatunde Raji Fashola Senate Building. The Vice-Chancellor noted ongoing improvements in policies, strengthened partnerships, the establishment of the Disability Support Office, inclusive education initiatives, enhanced health services, and collaborations that provide scholarships and sponsorships.

Reaffirming LASU’s commitment, she outlined the University’s vision of prosperity, social harmony, safety, and freedom for persons with special needs, and its mission to ensure equal access to opportunities and services for all. She commended stakeholders and partners for their efforts in promoting disability rights and expressed appreciation to everyone involved in the celebration.

In his address, the Head of Department, Educational Foundations and Counselling Psychology, Professor Ife Abodunrin, commended Lagos State University for its commitment to inclusivity, noting the establishment of the Special Education Unit within the department three years ago. He highlighted the admission of students with special needs across various faculties and the provision of suitable accommodation and supportive facilities that enable them to thrive.

Professor Abodunrin praised the University’s management for their dedication to supporting students with special needs and emphasised the importance of educational and workplace inclusion. He also stressed the need for strong community support, healthcare assistance, and appropriate academic support during classes and examinations, encouraging students and colleagues to help their peers with disabilities through note-taking, transcription, and timetable guidance.

The highlight of the event was the presentation of the “Legacy Award for Advancing Disability Support and Inclusive Education at LASU” and a book titled "_The Joy of Signing_" to the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, mni, NPOM. The event was graced by the Director, Sandwich Degree Programme, Professor John Adeogun; the Deputy Registrar, Disability Support Office, Mrs A.M. Afolami-Arojojoye represented by Mr Olalekan Lasisi; the Deputy Registrar, Non-Academic Staff Establishment, Mrs Morili Ola-Gbadamosi; members of staff from the Special Education Unit and the Disability Support Office; other senior members of staff; and students.

The International Day of Persons with Disabilities (IDPD), observed every 3rd of December, is a UN-established day to champion the rights, dignity, and well-being of persons with disabilities globally. It serves as a vital call to action for fostering a truly inclusive, accessible, and equitable world for individuals with disabilities.

title: Lagos State University Clarifies Hybrid Learning Model: Only 197 of 4,095 Courses Affected, Students not being Kept at Home
excerpt: The attention of the Lagos State University (LASU) Management has been drawn to a recent publication titled “Assessing LASU’s Online Classes Directive”, which presents a one-sided and, in many respects, misleading narrative about...
content:
The attention of the Lagos State University (LASU) Management has been drawn to a recent publication titled “Assessing LASU’s Online Classes Directive”, which presents a one-sided and, in many respects, misleading narrative about the university’s recent decision to transition large-capacity classes to virtual platforms.

The Lagos State University (LASU) Management hereby issues a clarification to correct significant misinformation circulating regarding its recently enhanced blended learning policy. Contrary to reports suggesting a full shift to online learning, the University affirms that only 197 out of a total of 4,095 courses offered across the institution are delivered primarily online. These are specifically large lectures with enrolments exceeding 400 students.

This targeted measure is designed to improve the quality of the learning experience for these high-enrolment courses and forms part of a strategic shift towards modern, blended pedagogy. The vast majority of tutorials, seminars, laboratory practicals, and smaller courses will continue as in-person sessions, and students are expected to be on campus for the core of their academic activities.

The University’s management regrets the concern caused by the mischaracterisation of the blended learning policy. The directive is a focused effort to manage large classes more effectively, a common challenge for leading universities in Nigeria and to ensure ease of learning.

The narrative that students are being told to ‘stay at home’ for online classes is factually incorrect and misleading. This policy affects less than 5% (about 197 courses out of 4095 courses offered) of the University’s total course offerings. Students are, and will remain fully engaged in campus life, with access to libraries, laboratories, sporting facilities, medical facilities, and the full spectrum of face-to-face (physical) teaching for the overwhelming majority of their timetabled activities.

This approach is consistent with practices at other forward-looking international and national universities, which similarly use digital platforms to supplement and enhance the delivery of content for large classes.

The blended learning policy is fully aligned with the National Universities Commission’s (NUC) drive to integrate e-learning into the fabric of Nigerian higher education. To ensure no student is disadvantaged, LASU has made significant investments in support infrastructure, including upgraded campus-wide Wi-Fi, dedicated ICT hubs, and a reliable on-campus power supply to mitigate connectivity issues, among other initiatives.

The Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, mni, NPOM, hereby reiterates the University’s commitment to transparency, as a University committed to excellence, we are duty-bound to adopt innovative teaching methods that serve our students best.

This precise data-driven approach for a small subset of our courses is a prudent academic decision, not an administrative shortcut. It allows us to optimise our physical resources while preparing our students for the digital world. We encourage our students and parents to seek accurate information through our official channels, and to view this policy not as a retreat from responsibility, but as a bold step toward a more resilient, inclusive, and future-ready LASU.

title: LASU Reaffirms Leadership in Academic Excellence, Compassion and Holistic Dvelopment with Inauguration of Mental Health Advocates
excerpt: The Counselling and Careers Unit of Lagos State University on Tuesday, 4th November 2025, inaugurated and trained a team of Mental Health Advocates - volunteer staff and students empowered with the knowledge, skills and awareness...
content:
The Counselling and Careers Unit of Lagos State University on Tuesday, 4th November 2025, inaugurated and trained a team of Mental Health Advocates - volunteer staff and students empowered with the knowledge, skills and awareness needed to promote positive mental health across the university community.

The training and inauguration ceremony, held at the Aderemi Makanjuola Lecture Theatre, was organised in collaboration with Mental Space Foundation Africa and aimed to address the growing concerns surrounding mental health among members of the LASU community.

In her keynote address, the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, mni, NPOM, described the initiative as both timely and deeply significant in tackling the rising challenges of mental health within the university environment. She noted that the pressures of academic pursuit, social expectations, and personal struggles often take a toll on emotional and psychological well-being.

Professor Olatunji-Bello, who was represented by the Director, Open and Distance Learning and Research Institute (ODLRI), Professor Adenike Boyo, said, “This event marks a powerful step forward,” she remarked. “It represents our collective commitment to break the silence, replace stigma with support, and ensure that no member of our university, families or friends walks alone in times of emotional distress.”

She reaffirmed that LASU remains a trailblazer not only in academic excellence but also in compassion, empathy, and holistic development. She explained that the newly inaugurated Mental Health Advocates would serve as peer supporters, listeners, and lighthouses, helping others navigate the storms of anxiety, depression, and related challenges.

Delivering the opening address, Dr Joseph Ayeni, Head of the Counselling and Careers Unit and host of the event, explained that the initiative stemmed from the desire to help students struggling with mental health issues. “The idea came up for students to help themselves, based on the reality that many are suffering from mental health challenges. We believe students can identify and support one another,” he said.

Dr Ayeni commended the Vice-Chancellor for her welfarist approach to leadership, noting that her approval and encouragement made the programme possible. He expressed confidence that the new advocates would make positive and lasting impact within the university community.

The training sessions featured lectures by Dr Olubukola Oyediji, who spoke on Mental Health and Its Antecedents, and Dr Ayeni, who delivered a presentation on Psychological First Aid. Both sessions equipped the new advocates with essential knowledge for their roles. The event also included a lively panel discussion, where participants engaged directly with the speakers and Ms Mojisola Ajayi, Founder of Mental Space Foundation Africa and a proud alumna of LASU.

Meanwhile, Dr Ayeni announced that a similar training and inauguration exercise would soon be held at the Epe Campus for staff and students.

title: Innovation at Work as LASU Redefines Learning Through Full Digital Integration
excerpt: In what can best be described as a defining moment for higher education in Nigeria, Lagos State University has taken a giant leap towards full digitalisation, setting the stage for a smarter, technology-driven academic experience....
content:
In what can best be described as a defining moment for higher education in Nigeria, Lagos State University has taken a giant leap towards full digitalisation, setting the stage for a smarter, technology-driven academic experience. The University has now gone fully digital, creating innovative measures that will enable students to comfortably take lectures online. This strategic move is aimed at strengthening LASU’s long-standing commitment to innovation, technology-based teaching, and modern learning delivery.

The landmark initiative is championed by the Office of the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academics), Professor Oseni Taiwo AFISI, and the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Administration), Professor Oluwatoyin ENIKUOMEHIN, who jointly convened a crucial meeting with Provost, Deans, Academic Directors, Heads of Departments, and course lecturers handling classes with over four hundred students.

The meeting, which was held at the Senate Chamber, first floor, Babatunde Raji Fashola Senate Building, LASU Main Campus, Ojo, Lagos, focused on the deployment and effective use of the University’s digital platforms, including the Learning Management System (LMS), DigiLearn, Zoom, and LASU Radio, for virtual teaching across faculties.

The Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academics), Professor Afisi, in his opening remarks, welcomed all participants and outlined the purpose of the meeting, stressing that the transition to virtual learning is not merely a response to modern trends, but a deliberate effort to enhance teaching and learning at the university. Supported by the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Administration), Professor Enikuomehin, he emphasised the directive that all classes with four hundred students and above should henceforth be conducted digitally in all faculties and schools.

The meeting featured key operational discussions on how these platforms will work in synergy to ensure a smooth experience for both lecturers and students.

The Radio Manager, Dr Jamiu YAHYA, assured participants of the readiness of LASU Radio 95.7 F.M to broadcast lectures as part of the digital initiative. He stated that lecturers would be guided by standard broadcasting rules, including appropriate time management, call-in sessions for student interaction, and adherence to professional presentation standards. The radio broadcast, he noted, is designed as a supplementary platform to enhance accessibility and serve as added value for large classes.

To ensure proper coordination, Mr Dayo OLUBAKIN and Mr J.B. ASHIYANBI have been appointed as Radio Monitoring Managers to oversee activities on LASU Radio 95.7f.m, while Mr Bolaji ODEDIRAN will serve as the Zoom Manager. Furthermore, the University’s Zoom package has been significantly upgraded to accommodate over 2,000 participants and provides unlimited cloud storage all thanks to the visionary support of the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi Ibilola OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM, whose commitment continues to drive digital transformation at Lagos State University.

During the meeting, the Dean, Faculty of Social Sciences, Professor Olufemi LAWAL demonstrated a sample Zoom class to illustrate key expectations for virtual conduct, including lecturers’ dress codes, digital comportment, and engagement techniques during online lectures. On his part, Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Administration), Professor Enikuomehin conducted a live demonstration of the LASU DigiLearn platform web.lasu.edu.ng/digilearn, walking participants through its features and explaining how Deans, Directors, and Heads of Departments could seamlessly navigate and utilise the platform. He further explained that the DigiLearn Forum allows real-time interaction between instructors and students, creating opportunities for feedback, assessments, and discussions.

Professor Enikuomehin also announced that selected venues have been equipped for recording lectures, and lecturers are required to make bookings before use. He emphasised that Telegram and other unverified applications are not approved for official teaching activities, as the University has provided verified and secured platforms for all virtual engagements. Instructors are to log in for digital lectures using their PF numbers and passwords, while students are required to identify themselves with their surnames and matriculation numbers.

The Dean, Faculty of Computing and Information Science, Professor Benjamin S. ARIBISALA provided further expert insights, recommending that lecturers and students must ensure a stable internet connection, and advise students to take screenshots during lectures to capture key points, and encourage students to participate in online quizzes to promote engagement and consistent attendance. He also advised lecturers to mute students during sessions except when they indicate interest to speak by raising their hands virtually.

In a major announcement, Professor Oseni Afisi revealed that the University’s Virtual Laboratory (VLAB) will officially become operational from Monday, 3rd November 2025, marking another milestone in LASU’s journey toward full digital transformation. He charged all Deans and Heads of Departments to take responsibility for the smooth implementation and effectiveness of e-lectures across their respective faculties and Departments.

With these developments, Lagos State University has positioned itself as a leader in digital education in Nigeria, setting a benchmark for technology-driven academic practices. The University’s integrated approach in combining online platforms, digital radio, and interactive learning tools, reflects its unwavering resolve to provide a world-class educational experience for its students.

Through the vision and leadership of the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ibiyemi Ibilola Olatunji-Bello, mni, NPOM, and the dedication of the university’s management team, LASU continues to prove that innovation, technology, and academic excellence can coexist to redefine the future of learning.

Indeed, Lagos State University is not just embracing technology, it is shaping the digital future of higher education in Nigeria and beyond.

title: UNDP/UNIPOD Equipment Installation and Training for Staff and Students in LASU
excerpt: The Lagos State University Innovation Hub, has once again demonstrated its leadership in technology-driven education and creative innovation as representatives of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), and UniPod Africa...
content:
The Lagos State University Innovation Hub, has once again demonstrated its leadership in technology-driven education and creative innovation as representatives of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), and UniPod Africa visited the University for the installation of world-class digital equipment, train staff and students on the usage.

The training and installation training session, held on Monday, 27th October 2025, at the LASU Innovation Hub, Awori House, LASU Main Campus, Ojo, Lagos, marked a major milestone in the university's innovation journey, as the institution joined seven other Nigerian academic institutions benefiting from the UNDP/UniPod Initiative - a project designed to equip tertiary institutions with state-of-the-art creative and digital technology infrastructure.

At a brief meeting with staff and students, Manager, Lagos State University Innovation Hub, Professor Tunji AZEEZ, welcomed the UNDP team, applauded the initiative and described it as a transformative opportunity that will expand the frontiers of innovation and skill-based learning at the university. His words "The LASU Innovation Hub is designed to bring all related creatives under one umbrella as a place where ideas are not only imagined, but built, tested, and brought to life. This collaboration with UNDP and UniPod strengthens our vision of making LASU a leading Centre for digital innovation, research, and entrepreneurship", he remarked.

Professor Azeez also used the opportunity to express profound appreciation to the Vice-Chancellor, Lagos State University, Professor Ibiyemi Ibilola OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM, ably represented by the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academics), Professor Oseni Taiwo AFISI, for her unwavering commitment to positioning LASU as a model for innovation and excellence.

He further extended heartfelt gratitude to the donor and Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), Princess Adejoke ORELOPE-ADEFULIRE, for her generous support, and to the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) for consistent partnership and investment in youth-focused innovation across Nigeria. “Our gratitude to the Vice-Chancellor, our donor, and the UNDP can not be overstated. Their support has made it possible for LASU students to access cutting-edge facilities that will ignite creativity, inspire innovation, and produce solutions with global impact" he stated

The installation exercise was led by Engr TOCHUKWU, who headed a three-man technical team from UNDP, tasked with setting up the equipment across all eight UniPods in Nigeria, with LASU being one of the key beneficiaries.

Students from diverse academic backgrounds including Computer Science, Engineering, Theatre and Film Arts, Physics, and Mass Communication, among others participated actively in the session, which featured a “Train-the-Trainer" model designed to empower participants to pass on their knowledge to others.

The participants were grouped into three specialised units to facilitate hands-on learning:

• Electronics and Robotics Group, which is focused on programming and robotic assembly.

• The 3D Printing Technology Group introduced to advanced 3D modeling and additive manufacturing.

• CO₂ Laser and Vinyl Cutting Group is trained in precision cutting, engraving, and creative fabrication techniques.

With the successful installation of these globally recognised technological systems, LASU now boasts some of the most advanced creative and fabrication equipment available in higher education in the world.

Core UniPod volunteers, comprising trained staff and students, will continue to oversee the use of these facilities while ensuring continuous training across faculties in order to reinforce LASU’s commitment to sustainability, safety, and skill transfer.

The milestone underscores the university's strategic drive to merge academia, technology, and creativity in solving real-world problems and preparing students for global opportunities.

The LASU Innovation Hub is where ideas grow, stories inspire, and innovation thrives.

title: LASU Queens ready to take the World by Storm as Team Represents Africa at 2025 FISU University World Cup Football
excerpt: – Competition starts Tuesday, 16th September 2025, in Dalian, China As hostilities get underway at the forthcoming Fédération Internationale du Sport Universitaire (FISU) World University Games in Dalian, China, the African...
content:
– Competition starts Tuesday, 16th September 2025, in Dalian, China

As hostilities get underway at the forthcoming Fédération Internationale du Sport Universitaire (FISU) World University Games in Dalian, China, the African champions, Lagos State University (LASU) women’s football team, will be representing Africa in the Women’s World Football fiesta.

The football event will commence from Tuesday, 16th to Sunday, 28th September 2025.

The 2025 FISU University World Cup Football is taking place in Dalian, China:

Group A

- Shanghai University of Sport(Host)

- Lagos State University(Nigeria)

- University of the Extreme South of Santa Catarina(Brazil)

- University of Valencia(Spain)

Group B

- Beijing Normal University(China)

- University of Sydney(Australia)

- Polytechnic University of Hauts-de-France(France)

- Laval Rouge et Or(Canada)

The top two teams from each group will qualify for the semi-finals, and the winners of the two semi-final matches will progress to the final.

The LASU Queens held their final training session on Saturday, 13th September 2025, at the Sports Centre, LASU Main Campus, Ojo, Lagos, as the team was scheduled to depart for Dalian, China, on Sunday, 14th September 2025.

LASU CIPR monitored the training of the ladies and can report that the players are in high spirits, ready to take the world by storm. The team worked on their tactics, as well as a penalty shoot-out session, to round off preparations.

The Assistant Captain of the team, Busayo Kushoro, expressed confidence that the team would perform well, based on their team spirit, the effort invested, and the quality of training.

"We are excited to be carrying the banner of LASU and representing Africa. We look forward to a great competition. The training has not been easy, but we have put in our best," the final-year Marketing student quipped.

When asked about their opponents, the right full-back retorted that they are not afraid of any team, as they intend to take each game as it comes. She called on the LASU football-loving community to keep praying and to throw their support behind the team.

On a final note, Kushoro strongly believes that the LASU team could go on to spring a surprise, saying they have watched tapes of their opponents and are convinced they are not better than the African Queens.

Recall that the LASU Queens secured the sole ticket to represent Africa by defeating co-host, University of Lagos (UNILAG), in the final match of the All Africa University Games, held in September 2024 at the LASU Sports Centre, Main Campus, Ojo, Lagos.

title: Approved Calendar for the 2025/2026 Academic Session
excerpt: The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, mni, NPOM, on behalf of the University Senate, has granted executive approval for the Academic Calendar for the 2025/2026 Academic Session as follows:
content:
The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, mni, NPOM, on behalf of the University Senate, has granted executive approval for the Academic Calendar for the 2025/2026 Academic Session as follows:

FIRST SEMESTER

• Monday, 15th September – Friday, 3rd October 2025: Registration for new students (3 weeks).

• Monday, 6th October – Friday, 19th December 2025: Resumption and registration for returning students, alongside the commencement of lectures for both new and returning students (11 weeks).

• Monday, 22nd December 2025 – Friday, 2nd January 2026: End-of-year break (2 weeks).

• Monday, 5th January – Friday, 9th January 2026: Revision and late registration (with a penalty fee of ₦5,000) (1 week).

• Monday, 12th January – Friday, 6th February 2026: Examinations (4 weeks).

• Monday, 9th February – Friday, 20th February 2026: Grading and uploading of results (2 weeks).

• Monday, 23rd February – Friday, 27th February 2026: Departmental and Faculty consideration, uploading of corrections, ICT processing of results, collation, and Senate meeting for the approval of results (1 week).

New students will spend a total of 24 weeks in the first semester while returning students will spend a total of 21 weeks.

SECOND SEMESTER

• Monday, 2nd March – Friday, 22nd May 2026: Resumption, registration and lectures for new and returning students (12 weeks).

• Monday, 25th May – Friday, 5th June 2026: Examinations (4 weeks).

• Monday, 8th June – Friday, 19th June 2026: Grading and uploading of results (2 weeks).

• Monday, 22nd June – Friday, 26th June 2026: Departmental and Faculty consideration, uploading of corrections and ICT processing of results (1 week).

• Monday, 29th June – Friday, 3rd July 2026: Collation of results and Senate meeting for consideration and approval of results (1 week).

• Monday, 6th July 2026: End-of-session break commences.

The Second Semester shall be for a duration of 20 weeks.

• Sessional Break: Monday, 6th July – Friday, 2nd October 2026 (3 months).

• New Session: The 2026/2027 Academic Calendar commences on Monday, 6th October 2026.

The executive approval granted by the Vice-Chancellor was based on the recommendation of the Committee of Provost, Deans and Directors (COPDD) held on Thursday, 11th September 2025.
